title: Chapter 8 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of CSS selectors, combinators, pseudo‑classes/elements, and specificity!

questions.question:
Which selector targets all `

` elements with the class `intro`?
questions.explanation: `p.intro` (no space) selects paragraphs that have the class intro.

questions.question: What does `h1, h2, h3` do?
options: Selects h1 inside h2 inside h3
Selects all h1, h2, and h3 elements
Selects the first h1, then h2, then h3
Selects only the first matching element
questions.explanation: Comma grouping applies the rule to all listed selectors.

questions.question: The child combinator is represented by the ______ character.
questions.explanation: `>` selects direct children only.

questions.question: Which selector will select the `<li>` elements that are direct children of `<ul>` with class `menu`?
questions.explanation: `.menu > li` targets only direct children.

questions.question: What does `h2 + p` select?
options:
Any

that is a child of
questions.explanation: `+` is the adjacent sibling combinator, targeting the very next sibling.

questions.question:
`div ~ p` selects all `

` elements that are siblings of a `

` and come after it.
questions.explanation: The general sibling combinator `~` selects all following siblings of the specified type.

questions.question: Which attribute selector matches any element that has a `title` attribute regardless of its value?
questions.explanation: `[attr]` matches presence only.

questions.question: How would you select all `<a>` elements whose `href` ends with `.pdf`?
questions.explanation: `$=` matches attribute values ending with the specified string.

questions.question: What does `input[type="text" i]` select?
options: Only inputs with exactly type="text" in lowercase
Inputs with type="text" case‑insensitively (e.g., TEXT, Text)
questions.explanation: The `i` flag makes the value comparison case‑insensitive.

questions.question: Which pseudo‑class applies when an element is being clicked and held?
questions.explanation: `:active` matches during the activation (e.g., mouse button down).

questions.question: The `:focus` pseudo‑class is only triggered by keyboard navigation, not mouse clicks.
questions.explanation: `:focus` applies regardless of input method. `:focus-visible` can be used to differentiate.

questions.question: What does `li:nth-child(odd)` select?
options: The first odd‑numbered list item in the document
All `<li>` elements that are at odd positions among their siblings (1st, 3rd, 5th...)
questions.explanation: `nth-child(odd)` selects elements whose index is odd (1,3,5...).

questions.question: Which pseudo‑class targets the last child of a parent?
questions.explanation: `:last-child` matches an element that is the last child of its parent.

questions.question: What does `p:not(.special)` mean?
options:
All `

` elements that are not having the class `special`
The first paragraph without class special
All paragraphs inside an element without class special
questions.explanation: `:not()` excludes elements matching the inner selector.

questions.question: What must you include for `::before` to render?
questions.explanation: The `content` property is required; it can be empty string.

questions.question: Which pseudo‑element targets the first letter of a paragraph?
questions.explanation: `::first-letter` styles the first character.

questions.question: What does `::selection` allow you to style?
options: The first line of an element
The text the user has highlighted with the mouse
The placeholder text of an input
The bullet of a list item
questions.explanation: `::selection` applies to the portion of the document that is selected.

questions.question: Which specificity is correct for the selector `#main .container li.active`?
questions.explanation: ID=1 (#main), classes=2 (.container, .active), type=1 (li). So (0,1,2,1).

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: #header is an ID, which beats class or type selectors.

questions.question: An inline style has specificity:
questions.explanation: Inline styles (style attribute) contribute a=1.

questions.question: The universal selector `*` adds to specificity.
questions.explanation: `*` contributes no specificity.

questions.question: When two rules have equal specificity, which one wins?
questions.explanation: If specificity is equal, the last rule in source order takes precedence.

questions.question: What is a recommended practice to avoid specificity battles?
questions.explanation: Low specificity with classes makes overriding manageable.

questions.question: What is BEM?
options: A naming convention for CSS classes to make them clear and unique
questions.explanation: BEM (Block Element Modifier) helps create unique, descriptive class names.

questions.question: Which pseudo‑class is useful for styling form inputs that have focus but only when the keyboard is used?
questions.explanation: `:focus-visible` shows focus only when the browser deems it necessary (e.g., keyboard navigation).
